import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.feature_selection import f_classif
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Check if any mechanism exists (very low probability)
    if np.random.rand() > 0.8:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Find strongest features by t-test
    t_stats = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if feats.types[i] == 'derived':
            continue  # Skip derived features for driver selection
        y0 = feats.x[feats.y==0, i]
        y1 = feats.x[feats.y==1, i]
        t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(y0, y1, equal_var=False)
        t_stats.append((abs(t_stat), fid))
    
    # Sort by absolute t-statistic
    t_stats.sort(reverse=True)
    
    # Select top candidates
    candidates = [fid for _, fid in t_stats[:20]]
    
    # Remove near-duplicates
    to_remove = set()
    for i, fid1 in enumerate(candidates):
        for j, fid2 in enumerate(candidates[i+1:], i+1):
            if fid1 in to_remove or fid2 in to_remove:
                continue
            corr = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, feats.column(fid1)], 
                              feats.x[:, feats.column(fid2)])[0,1]
            if abs(corr) >= 0.6:
                to_remove.add(fid2)
    
    candidates = [fid for fid in candidates if fid not in to_remove]
    
    # If we have enough candidates, select top ones as drivers
    # Ensure we don't exceed MAX_DRIVERS
    drivers = tuple([fid for _, fid in t_stats[:min(MAX_DRIVERS, len(candidates))]])
    
    # For columns, use all significant features
    columns = tuple(candidates)
    
    # For products, consider pairs with high correlation
    products = []
    for i, fid1 in enumerate(columns):
        for j, fid2 in enumerate(columns[i+1:], i+1):
            corr = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, feats.column(fid1)], 
                              feats.x[:, feats.column(fid2)])[0,1]
            if abs(corr) >= 0.6:
                products.append((fid1, fid2))
    
    # Loadings - weight by effect size
    loadings = {}
    for fid in columns:
        idx = feats.column(fid)
        y0 = feats.x[feats.y==0, idx]
        y1 = feats.x[feats.y==1, idx]
        effect_size = np.mean(y1) - np.mean(y0)
        loadings[fid] = effect_size
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=tuple(products), loadings=loadings)
